course: There is something I find quite hilarious due to how backwards it is in this course. In a course of utmost importance like CS 201, the instructors held our hands by teaching C++ for 10 weeks. Yes, C++, the language that has an absurd, incredible number of mature educational content all over the world. But in this course, CS 223, where Verilog is crucial for your letter grade, you are pretty much left on your own. Yes, Verilog, the language that has absolutely terrible, disgusting resources anywhere you scour online. I thought people were exaggerating and surely any language would have great ways to learn existing online. No, they were right, it is a massive pain to learn Verilog. And even more so to learn SystemVerilog, which has EVEN SCARCER resources online. I seriously don't even get who on earth uses SystemVerilog instead of Verilog. But there are two reasons to rejoice still: The book DDCA has most HDL excerpts that you're gonna need, and at least we don't go anywhere near the atrocity that is VHDL. Also, I despise Vivado, can't wait to nuke it off my hard disk ASAP.
